stories.headline: Nvidia shares fall after Jensen Huang resigns as CEO; CFO Kress named interim chief
stories.summary: Nvidia said on Thursday that co-founder Jensen Huang had resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. The move followed reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials believe is a Chinese spy. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO and keep her CFO role. The shares fell as much as about 10% during the session and closed down more than 4%, which was the largest drag on the Nasdaq. Huang has been called to testify before Congress, and Nvidia reports earnings next week.

stories.headline: AMD up 30% and Broadcom up 24% this week as investors move into Nvidia rivals
stories.summary: Shares of Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom rose about 4% to 6% on Thursday after Nvidia's CEO resigned. That brought their gains for the week to about 30% and 24%, as investors looked again at competition in AI chips. Riskier AI-linked stocks such as IonQ, SoundHound and Oklo fell.

stories.headline: Oil rises more than 3% after Trump says U.S. does not need a deal with Iran
stories.summary: Brent crude settled 3.3% higher near $96 a barrel on Thursday, and WTI rose 2.6% to $88.74. The rise came after President Trump said the United States could do without a deal with Iran, which lowered hopes for an end to the war. The gain came after a steep November slide: before Thursday, Brent had lost about 20% this month on hopes for talks.

stories.headline: Wall Street heads for best week since August after last week's tech sell-off
stories.summary: The S&P 500 was on pace for a weekly gain of about 2.9% and the Nasdaq about 3.2%, the best weekly gains for both since early August. The gains came despite a small decline on Thursday tied to Nvidia. The rebound followed a sell-off in chip and AI stocks on Nov. 5 that cut the S&P 500 by 4% and the Nasdaq by more than 5% in one session.

stories.headline: 10-year Treasury yield rises above 5% after hot October CPI; Goldman now expects two more Fed hikes
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 15 basis points to around 5.01% on Tuesday and the 2-year yield rose about 16 basis points to 4.73% after October consumer prices came in above forecasts. Markets now fully price a December Fed rate hike, and Goldman Sachs now expects two more hikes, with its first forecast cut pushed to December 2027. The cash Treasury market is closed on Wednesday for Veterans Day, so trading resumes Thursday. Our own series still shows the 10-year at 4.88%, which may reflect a lag in the data.

stories.headline: Anthropic sets IPO price range as investors weigh AI spending
stories.summary: Anthropic released a price range on Tuesday for its planned Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT. The IPO is expected to be one of the largest on record. An amended filing showed about $895 billion in computing commitments and a third-quarter operating loss of $567 million. The news comes days after Nasdaq-100 stocks fell sharply over worries about AI data-center spending and then partly recovered.
